title: Harvard Taiwanese Cultural Society
content_html:
The Harvard Taiwanese Cultural Society (TCS) is a student-run organization at Harvard College dedicated to promoting the culture and heritage of Taiwan and Taiwanese Americans. Alumni records on the organization’s archived website document members as far back as the Class of 1995, placing the group’s founding in the early-to-mid 1990s, though an exact founding year is not confirmed in first-party sources. TCS describes its vision as fostering “a community in which people of all backgrounds can share, explore, and further develop an interest in Taiwanese culture,” and is recognized by Harvard College as one of the university’s student affinity groups.

The organization runs a wide range of programming throughout the academic year, including weekly Wednesday dinners, cultural events such as dumpling-making, social events like karaoke, and its signature annual Night Market — a fall-semester event designed to replicate the atmosphere of Taiwanese night markets, featuring food from Taiwanese caterers, student performances, and carnival-style games. TCS also maintains a “sib-fam” mentorship structure that pairs members into smaller family-like groups to build closer relationships within the broader organization. The group’s motto, “Small Island, Big Family,” reflects its emphasis on tight-knit community.

TCS maintains an active Instagram account (@harvardtcs) and Facebook page, and has a website at harvardtcs.com. Its connection to the wider Taiwanese American student community is reflected in its longstanding participation in the Boston Intercollegiate Taiwanese Students Association (BITSA), with documented involvement dating to BITSA’s founding era in the late 1990s.
